item.title: Reinstalling WSL2: Migrating a Research and Development Environment from Ubuntu 22.04 to Ubuntu 26.04
item.description:
Recently, I reinstalled the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2), migrated my existing Ubuntu 22.04 development environment to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and reconfigured my research and development tools, including C++, CUDA, Python, and GitHub.

The immediate reason for this reinstallation was disk space. My computer has only one 1 TB SSD, and the old WSL installation was taking up nearly 500 GB. Upon investigation, I found that the problem wasn’t entirely due to the WSL virtual disk itself, but rather to the long-term accumulation of research code, compilation outputs, and numerical experiment results.

I’ve decided to take this opportunity to reorganize my entire development environment and document any noteworthy configuration details.

item.title: Software for Windows 11
item.description:
Software

  • Office 365: Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OneNote, and Outlook.

  • Foxit: PDF reader available under an XMU license.

  • Chrome: Web browser.

  • Zotero: Research assistant.

  • Netch: Proxy client.

  • SSTap: Proxy client (preferred).

  • MATLAB: Mathematical programming language available under an XMU license.

  • Typora: Markdown editor.

  • XMind: Flowchart editor.

  • VS Code: The best editor.

  • CloudMusic: Music player.

  • Tencent Meeting: Video conferencing platform.

  • Zoom: Video conferencing platform.

  • Anki: Flashcard tool.

  • TranslucentTB: Taskbar customization tool available from the Microsoft Store.

  • QuickLook: File preview tool available from the Microsoft Store.

  • Baidu Netdisk: Cloud storage service.
